subject: Plain-language DPA snippets for hosting regions & console microcopy
messages:
From: Jose Santos <j.santos@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: concise DPA language for hosted API + console tooltip

Hi Sean,

Quick one from our side — Acme's legal team is finishing a vendor review and asked for a short, customer-facing DPA summary we can share with our security council. They want:

- A 2-3 sentence plain-language description of what data Redwood processes for hosted API customers (and what we don't)
- A brief explanation of cross-border transfers and where data may be routed/processed (high level; no org-level secrets)
- One-line tooltip copy for your console that explains "What does Redwood mean by data residency?"

They also want to see a recent subprocessor list and a simple note about encryption/KMS usage.

Attached is our vendor questionnaire response (we'll need the snippets by EOD Friday so we can circulate to the council next week). Can you point us to a ready-made public snippet or draft something short we can insert?

Thanks,
Jose
Legal Operations — ACME Corp

Attachments: acme_vendor_questionnaire.pdf (stub)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jose Santos <j.santos@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: concise DPA language for hosted API + console tooltip

Jose — thanks for the clear ask. I put a first-pass below (short bullets + one-line tooltip). I'm copying Laura and Kim to confirm legal/consistency. Vivek, FYI on subprocessors.

Draft plain-language DPA snippet (2–3 sentences):
"Redwood processes customer-supplied input and generates model outputs to provide hosted inference services. We do not use customer inputs to train models or improve shared models; customer data is isolated for the duration of processing and retention follows customer-configured settings. Data may be processed in the cloud regions you select and temporarily routed to nearby regions for availability and latency — details and region options are listed in our console and DPA."

Console tooltip (one line):
"Data residency: where your API requests are processed; select a region to keep processing and short-term cache in that geography."

Subprocessor note (one line):
"We use a small set of cloud and networking providers for compute and storage; a current list of subprocessors is published in our DPA and subprocessor map."

Attachments: I attached console_tooltip_drafts.md with two shorter variants and redwood_dpa_summary_v2.docx with the above text plus an expanded paragraph for legal review.

Next steps: Laura/Kim — can you review for legal accuracy and add anything about KMS/HSM or SOC 2 references? Jose — if you need more formal DPA language for your procurement team I can escalate to Contracts for a tailored extract.

Best,
Sean
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: console_tooltip_drafts.md (stub), redwood_dpa_summary_v2.docx (stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Jose Santos <j.santos@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 13:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: concise DPA language for hosted API + console tooltip

Thanks Sean — good baseline. A few legal edits and a stronger customer-facing sentence about transfers:

- Change "temporarily routed to nearby regions" -> "may be routed to compatible regions to meet availability and latency requirements; we honor customer region selections for primary processing and short-term cache."
- Add explicit callout about encryption: "All in-transit traffic is encrypted (TLS) and customer data at rest in hosted environments can be protected using customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) where available."
- For the subprocessor sentence, spell out that the list is "published and updated quarterly" and include a link to the map.

I've updated redwood_dpa_summary_v2.docx with the edits and added a short paragraph that references our SOC 2 Type II report. Jose — feel free to use the edited copy; if Procurement needs a vendor-signed DPA we can route that next.

Laura
VP, Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_summary_v2.docx (updated stub), subprocessor-map-20270509.xlsx (stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jose Santos <j.santos@acme.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: concise DPA language for hosted API + console tooltip

Jose — here's an even shorter customer-facing paragraph you can drop into the vendor questionnaire or slide deck (single paragraph, plain language):

"Redwood processes only the data you send to our hosted API to return requested outputs. We do not train models on customer inputs. You can choose a processing region in the console; we encrypt data in transit and provide options for customer-managed keys. A current list of subprocessors and our SOC 2 report are available on request or via the DPA link."

Tooltip variants included in console_tooltip_drafts.md:
- Variant A (short): "Data residency: choose where requests are processed."
- Variant B (longer): "Data residency: select a region to keep inference processing and short-lived caches in that geography; this does not change where models are developed."

Kimberly
Head of Product Marketing
Redwood Inference

Attachments: console_tooltip_drafts.md (shortlist stub)
